targets.c1td59kv1u1aegl1dskx3h: W-02 is Ari’s sizing sheet. It opens on Fennel’s requests as the teams set them, and counts the nodes those requests need if the Pods are packed as tightly as they will go, plus one spare node so that Fennel can lose a node, as it did at 03:04. Each Pod’s outline is what it reserves, and the solid fill inside it is what it used at last Friday’s rush. There is no target to reach; here are three things to notice:
targets.c1m724pj3x0oj618frzjl: THE NODES, PACKED AS TIGHTLY AS THEY GO
targets.c5xptny10c84gf1vx57yd: ROOM FOR PODS ON THE RENTED NODES
targets.cn2e5s08zv0ze1k155wx: W-02’s bar headed “Room for Pods on the rented nodes” shows what the Pods used, and splits the room they don’t use into two kinds. The first is room that no Pod has reserved, either because there are more nodes than the reservations need or because the room is stranded in pieces too small for any Pod. The second is room that Pods have reserved and don’t use, because their requests are bigger than the service needs. The “less than a third busy” on Ari’s dashboard counts both kinds together.
targets.c1e8gtyv1qdgbru1rmxamf: If you’re billed per Pod, the picture shifts, but the lesson stays the same. In most setups you pay for the machines; a few per-Pod options bill for what each Pod requests while it runs, not for what it uses. So padding costs money there too, Pod by Pod. And not every fully managed mode bills per Pod: some still bill per machine.
